speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To better assist you, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The onset of vertigo this morning that is constant and alleviated by diphenhydramine is very suggestive of a vestibular issue. Given your recent garlic intake and the severity of the spinning sensation, have you experienced any sudden hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or severe headache?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
